Girija-Narasiṁha
(‘Man-lion [incarnation] emerging out of a mountain cave’)
------------------------------------------
Nṛsiṁha or नरसिṁह is the fourth in the series of the ten incarnations of विष्णु generally known as ‘Daśāvatāras’. His head is that of a lion (= siṁha) whereas the rest of the body is that of a human being ( = नर).
As per the stories of the Bhāgavata (7.8.18-23) and the Viṣṇupurāṇa (1.32) he emerged out of a pillar in the court-hall of the demon-king हिरण्यकशिपु. However in some iconographical works, he is described as having emerged out of cave in a hill (giri = hill, ja = born or emerge) like an infuriated lion in a flash of blinding light. Hence the name गिरिज-नरसिṁह.
In this form he is shown alone, without लक्ष्मी or प्रह्लाद. He may have two arms or four arms. In the latter posture, the upper two hands are holding the usual emblems of Viṣṇu—the conch and the discus—whereas the two lower hands are thrown forward to seize हिरण्यकशिपु.
The complexion of this form is des-cribed as white and the garments red. The crown on the head is of the karaṇḍa-makuṭa (honeycomb) type.
